source_row.rationale: Verbal orders carry a higher inherent risk of miscommunication or error (due to potential mishearing, accents, background noise, or other factors) compared to written or electronic orders, so best practice and many facility policies restrict their use to situations of genuine clinical urgency, where the time-sensitivity justifies this increased risk, with read-back verification required when they are used.
source_row.source_detail: Rationale for Restricting Verbal Order Use
source_row.source_name: The Joint Commission — Verbal Order Policy and Safety Rationale
source_row.stem: A hospital policy restricts verbal medication orders to situations of clinical urgency, discouraging their routine use for non-urgent situations, and a provider questions why this restriction exists when verbal orders seem quicker and just as reliable as written ones.
